regime_context: Canada/TSX sector landscape shows broad eligible leadership (9 of 16 themes above the absolute-trend gate), with resource-heavy themes (Base Metals & Copper, Oil & Gas Producers, Gold Miners, Silver & Royalties) occupying the top four ranks. The rotation is broad (0.56 eligible fraction) but not one-narrative and not directional: absorption is low (0.30), and the leader's durability_bar (0.51) with mean-revert Hurst tag suggests momentum is thin. Track record (n=96) shows hits 65.6% but directional accuracy only 34.4%, meaning calls have not translated into correct directional reads — conviction must be low.
emerging_watch: Watching Gold Miners (XGD.TO) at rank 3, score 1.16, eligible but with breadth only 0.333 and durability_bar 0.49. The condition to retire this watch: XGD.TO closes in the top 2 ranks of momentum for 10 consecutive sessions while breadth (fraction of constituents above their trend) rises above 0.50 — that would mark a confirmed handoff from base metals/energy into gold; if breadth stays below 0.40 and score slips below 0.8 by the next check, the watch is retired.

theses.subject: Base Metals & Copper
theses.thesis: Top-ranked theme with score 1.74 and eligible trend-gate. Breadth 0.556 is mid-range and crowding_z 0.8 is uncrowded, so the leadership is real but not reflexive. The detector's only validated edge is drawdown control via the trend gate, which this theme passes. The case is that the resource narrative retains staying power over a modest horizon even if momentum itself has no forward return edge.
evidence: hurst_tag mean-revert flags low-trend health, not a momentum confirmation
theses.dissent: Hurst tag is mean-revert and durability_bar is only 0.51, implying the leadership is already decaying; copper/base metals often reverse sharply on global growth scares and are highly sensitive to a macro narrative that is unscheduled-surprise-heavy (0.40 share).

falsifier.text: XBM.TO closes below its 50-day moving average for 5 consecutive sessions before the 30-day check-by date

theses.subject: Oil & Gas Producers
theses.thesis: Rank 2, score 1.55, eligible, with the strongest durability_bar (0.64) and best breadth (0.643) in the eligible set. This leg (durability + breadth) supports a view that energy producers are a sturdier trend than base metals, albeit with a crowded_z near 1.0 worth a size-down tilt.
theses.dissent: Oil & gas is a macro-beta call on crude and OPEC/geopolitics, not a clean micro trend; with unscheduled_share at 0.40 the theme is vulnerable to headline whiplash, and the high crowding_z signals the trade is discovered.

falsifier.text: XEG.TO lags the S&P/TSX by more than 8% before the 30-day check-by date

theses.subject: Utilities & Renewables
theses.thesis: Rank 7, score -0.067, eligible but near-zero momentum with a crowding_z of -0.77 and breadth 0.417. The trend gate is open, but the detector's own backtest verdict says momentum rank is not alpha and the trend gate is only a risk-control leg. For a theme with no momentum and no crowding support, there is no reason to lean overweight; avoid is the cleaner directional call.
evidence: durability_bar 0.61 but hurst_tag trend suggests slow grind without upside follow-through
theses.dissent: Defensive yield themes like utilities can outperform during risk-off macro environments, and the macro narrative (geopolitics share) could tilt defensive; avoiding may miss a defensive bid.

falsifier.text: XUT.TO rises more than 5% relative to the S&P/TSX before the 30-day check-by date

macro_narrative.note: market-level macro/policy/geo narrative flow; coincident, not per-theme, never a trigger
